relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: Retrieves the instruction metadata for the decoded opcode (BMI, index MOS65XX_INS_BMI). The insinfo.group_type field is MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP, which is non-INVALID and will trigger the first group assignment. Combined with the MOS65XX_AM_REL addressing mode, both group-writing branches will execute.

The second group assignment writes MOS65XX_GRP_BRANCH_RELATIVE to the hardcoded index 0 instead of detail->groups[detail->groups_count]. Since groups_count was already incremented to 1 by the first branch, groups_count becomes 2 after this block, but groups[1] is never written. The fix changes both assignments to use detail->groups[detail->groups_count] so each group is stored at its proper sequential index.

The uninitialized value from detail->groups[1] arrives as the id parameter. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value at this comparison, where the indeterminate heap content is used in a conditional branch. If the value passes the bounds check, it would also be used as an index into GroupNames at line 520.
After both group branches execute, groups_count=2 but groups[1] is uninitialized (vulnerable) or properly written (fixed).

edges.description: The hardcoded write index (0 instead of groups_count) causes groups[1] to remain uninitialized after increment.
The uninitialized groups[1] value propagates through the harness iteration and cs_group_name dispatch to arrive as the id parameter at the sink.
